meta.title: Serverful vs Serverless: What Vercel Abstracts

views.label: Serverful: you run every layer
views.note: Each box is software someone must install, configure, patch, monitor and scale.

views.label: Serverless on Vercel
views.note: The same jobs still happen, but Vercel runs them. TPS ships only application code.

views.label: What Vercel replaces
views.note: Firewall, proxy and gateway collapse into Vercel's edge; containers become auto-scaled functions.

components.label: Firewall
components.explanation: Filters traffic before it reaches the server: open ports, IP rules, rate limits, web attack rules. On a VPS you choose, configure and update it yourself or buy a separate service.

components.label: Nginx
components.explanation: Terminates HTTPS (certificates must be renewed), serves or caches static files, and spreads requests across the app containers. Config, restarts and upgrades are your job.

components.label: API gateway
components.explanation: Routes each API path to the right service and applies authentication, quotas and request validation. Either a managed product such as Amazon API Gateway (billed separately) or custom code you maintain.

components.label: App container 1
components.explanation: One copy of the application running in Docker. Two or more copies are needed so one can restart or fail without taking the site down.

components.label: App container 2
components.explanation: Second copy for redundancy and extra capacity. Adding a third means resizing the VPS or adding servers by hand, and you pay for the reserved CPU/RAM even when idle.

components.label: Database
components.explanation: Self-hosted database: you handle backups, upgrades, disk space and failover.

components.label: Vercel edge network
components.sublabel: firewall + TLS + routing + CDN, built in
components.explanation: One managed layer does the firewall (WAF), HTTPS certificates, caching, routing and load distribution. No servers, ports or certificates for TPS to manage. Cached pages are answered here without running any code.

components.label: Vercel Functions
components.explanation: The application code (the form handler) runs here. Vercel starts more instances as traffic grows and fewer when it drops; concurrent requests can share an instance. Billed on active CPU, memory GB-hours and invocations, not on idle reserved capacity.

components.label: Managed database
components.explanation: Only if TPS needs its own records. The host handles backups, upgrades and scaling.

boundaries.label: VPS you rent: you patch the OS, Docker, scaling and monitoring
Serverless: Vercel runs everything except your code

cards.title: Serverful: you own
items: Firewall rules, TLS certificates, Nginx config
Capacity planning: reserved CPU/RAM billed even when idle

cards.title: Serverless: Vercel owns
items: Starting and stopping instances as traffic changes
Billing: plan + measured CPU, memory, invocations

cards.title: No universal winner
items: Serverful can be cheaper under heavy, steady load
Serverless suits uneven, modest traffic like the TPS launch
